newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgacom, unions sign landmark deal on job cuts.
newsitem.headline: Belgacom, unions sign landmark deal on job cuts.

text.p: Belgium's partially privatised state telephone company Belgacom said it signed a comprehensive deal with trade unions on Monday on a restructuring programme including redeployment and voluntary departure schemes.
In a statement, Belgacom said it would offer about 6,500 of its 26,000 workers early retirement from the age of 50 if they have a minimum of 20 years of service.
The deal will guarantee them 75 percent of their last monthly salary until the age of 60, the age at which workers are legally allowed to claim early retirement.
It added that voluntary departures would be spread over 18 months "so that customer service is not hindered".
It said between 4,000 and 6,000 employees will be affected by the redeployment programme, which has an estimated cost of 1.2 to 1.5 billion Belgian francs.
Belgacom is 49.9 percent owned by a consortium including Ameritech, Singapore Telecom, TeleDanmark and three Belgian investors.
